title: Elevators, toasters, and the birth of Java
summary: Ryan sits down with James Gosling, creator of Java at Sun Microsystems, to talk about the early networking friction that drove the need for interconnectedness, the stringent reliability requirements of consumer electronics companies that inspired the Java virtual machine, and the evolution of garbage collectors that allow Java to handle large-scale concurrent memory management.
llm_summary: In this interview, James Gosling explains how early networking hassles and the exacting reliability standards of consumer‑electronics makers pushed Sun to create a portable, robust runtime—what became the Java Virtual Machine. He also traces how Java’s garbage‑collector technology has evolved
